title: Delegate --notify room: pings fail: post rejects --allow-self since 3d4875f
description: Papercut pc2_9983998980bd6457 (codex, 2026-09-23T06:18Z). delegate-agent src/delegate_agent/notify.py notify_argv passes --allow-self for room targets (commit ba80dd7c), because post used to refuse from == to without it. Post removed the flag with the participant model (3d4875f, Sep 16): workspace mail skips the sending participant, and an explicit participant:<self> target is the self-send. Reproduced 2026-09-23 on a throwaway store: post send --to post-repo --allow-self exits 2, invalid_argument, unexpected argument. So every delegate room ping degrades to a failure. Fix is a design choice, not a flag deletion: dropping --allow-self alone makes the coordinator's own ping skip the coordinator (it is the resolved sender). Options: (a) delegate resolves its caller's participant (post participant show --json) and sends to participant:<id> when the room is the caller's own workspace; (b) delegate sends as its own participant (post participant bind --new, cached per workspace) so workspace routing includes the coordinator; (c) post re-adds a narrow include-sender flag for signal kind. Lean (b): the ping really is from delegate, and it keeps post's no-self-send rule intact. Not implemented overnight: it crosses a deliberate post identity decision and a second repo.

title: watch: self-echo suppression is per-room, so a multi-room watch rings itself
description: scan_batch suppresses a channel message when parsed.message.from == room, but the caller invokes it once per watched room.
